content:
I just noticed that docs#Equiv.ofBijective has this signature: {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (f : α → β) (hf : Function.Bijective f).

If I can supply hf, that automatically determines what f will be. I'd like to know more about why f has been coded as an explicit parameter instead of an implicit one.

Actually, it looks like the same thing is happening with docs#Set.BijOn.equiv, although I believe in that case if you have a proof h1 : Set.BijOn f α β, you can invoke h1.equiv and the explicit f parameter is implicitly filled in for you.

def has a different rule from theorem: if the non-prop parameter is only later mentioned in a prop parameter, it is still preferred to make it explicit. This is to help with two things

  • InfoView can display that parameter instead of just "..." for hypothesis
  • make match / cases easier to use on it. If it is implicit, you will have to use @ to get the parameter out
